newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil steady on German demand, U.S. weather.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil steady on German demand, U.S. weather.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums were steady in slow volume on Thursday, with heating oil supported by reasonable German demand and forecasts of lower temperatures in the United States, traders said.
A cargo of 0.2 percent sulphur gas oil (-5/-15) traded around unchanged at Feb IPE +10 cif Lorient.
German material was talked unchanged from Wednesday's late traded level of Feb IPE +$9.25 cif Hamburg.
"It's quiet because of the fair amount of material cleared out yesterday," a trader said. Others attibuted the slow pace to caution over recently choppy screen values.
Benchmark Feb IPE gas oil futures traded at 13.04 GMT up $3 at $216.50 a tonne, catching up with gains posted by crude after gas oil closed on Wednesday.
Barges saw moderate volumes and unchanged traded levels.
Refinery grade heating oil traded at Feb IPE +9 and +$9.50 for Rotterdam. Good storage material traded at Feb IPE +$7.75 fob Amsterdam.
Low sulphur diesel was bid at Feb +$14.
Ice problems persist in inland Germany and are seen lasting for the next week.
